Three steps.
Then get on with it.

No account to create. No cloud profile to babysit. Your controls, configured on your PC.

01

Find your hardware.

Add a device, give it a useful name, and move a control to confirm the right interface. Add another directly from the mapping editor.

02

Tell it what to do.

Choose the control, behavior and output. Start simple. Calibration, conditions and specific output choices are there when you need them.

03

Bind it. Make it yours.

Use the countdown to send a virtual test input. Save the profile, start outputs and verify the binding in your game.

06 / FAIR QUESTIONS

Before you
plug in.

A little clarity beats another forum rabbit hole.

Ask on GitHub
Is RigLogic really free?+

Yes. RigLogic is free, with Windows and Linux both planned for the first public release. You don’t need an account or a subscription to map controls, shape response curves, use Signal Labs or watch your inputs.

Support through Buy Me a Coffee is completely optional. It helps fund development; it is not a license or an unlock.

Is this only for sim racing?+

No. Use the same axis, button, switch and encoder tools with other supported controllers. Map a flight panel to virtual buttons, or a USB button pad to the shortcuts you use every day.

The target application needs to accept the keyboard or virtual-controller input you configure.

Will RigLogic be on Windows and Linux?+

Yes. Both are planned for the first public release. Linux is part of the launch, not an add-on for later.

On Windows, virtual joystick buttons and axes need a compatible x64 vJoy installation; keyboard shortcuts don’t. Linux will have its own setup instructions and system requirements alongside the download.

Use the package and instructions for your operating system. The example interfaces on this page illustrate the features, not a verified build for every platform.

Will it work with every game?+

Compatibility depends on the game, controller and driver. The game needs to accept the virtual joystick or keyboard commands you choose. Use the binding assistant to assign an output, then check it in the game.

For a handbrake wired through a wheelbase, keep the wheelbase visible for native steering and force feedback. Bind the processed handbrake separately, without a second raw handbrake binding.

What does the overlay actually measure?+

It shows the output RigLogic submits - not confirmation that the game received it. Red means active or recently active, gray means quiet, and amber means monitoring is unavailable. Each overlay stays with its own mapping.

Use borderless or windowed mode. Exclusive fullscreen and protected display modes can cover desktop overlays.

Will it forget everything if I move a USB cable?+

RigLogic matches saved devices using the hardware identifiers available to it, not just the USB port. Saved devices remain visible when disconnected, with their connection status and a Reconnect action.

When a match is unclear - such as two identical controllers without unique identifiers - you choose the correct interface. Reconnecting a saved device keeps its mappings and virtual assignments.

Does replay send my recording back to the game?+

No. Signal Labs replay is offline. Record an axis or a digital control, inspect what happened, then compare response curves, filters or timing without sending the recording to a game.

Analog recordings separate Raw input, Calibrated, Processed and Sent output. Digital recordings show input events and output timing. Captured data stays separate from the comparison, and you choose whether to apply a change.

Record for up to 30 minutes, subject to the event limit. Save recordings before closing the app.

THE SHORT ROUTE TO BETTER INPUTS

Your first mapping.

01

Open the player app.

When downloads open, choose the Windows or Linux package and follow its installation instructions. A new launch starts with outputs stopped.

02

Add the real device.

Click + → Add device. Give it a name, then move a control to confirm the correct interface. You can also add it from the mapping editor’s Device dropdown.

03

Choose control → behavior → output.

Detect the control, choose a held command, tap or axis behavior, then a virtual output or keyboard command. Manage virtual-output settings under Settings. On Windows, virtual joystick outputs need a compatible x64 vJoy installation; Linux uses its own platform setup.

04

Calibrate. Bind. Verify.

For an axis, capture released and full travel. Set a deadzone, then choose a response-curve preset or edit its points. Use … → Bind in game… for a countdown-generated virtual test input. Keep physical controls still; the helper cannot hide a visible raw controller.

05

Save it, then watch it.

Save your mapping and profile, start outputs, and verify the binding in the target application. Watch pins an independent overlay. Signal Labs records analog and digital mappings so you can compare changes offline. Save recordings before exiting.

Before driving

Pause rig motion during setup. Keep a wheelbase visible for native steering and force feedback. RigLogic’s output cleanup is not your motion platform’s emergency stop.

NOTHING TO SIGN INTO

A website.
Not another account.

This site has no analytics, advertising scripts, tracking pixels or contact forms. The interactive demos use simulated input and never access your hardware.

Your animation preference may be saved in local browser storage. No recording is uploaded. Links to GitHub and Buy Me a Coffee leave this site and are subject to those services’ own policies. A hosting provider can process ordinary connection logs.

RigLogic app diagnostics can include controller names, profile labels and file paths. Review them before sharing a support archive.
